---
title: "wgs_variant_extraction"
---

## Overview

This document extracts *Plasmodium falciparum* drug-resistance regions from whole-genome BAM files, runs PathWeaver/SeekDeep variant calling on those regions, and summarizes amino-acid changes by sample and country.

The workflow has three main code chunks:

1. The first R chunk creates the BED file used by PathWeaver. It reads the resistance amplicon table, keeps only rows marked as `Resistance`, removes genes that are not included in this run (`exo`, `pib7`, and `pph`), and selects chromosome, start, and end coordinates. It then builds the target name in the format expected by SeekDeep, for example `Pf3D7_01_v3-194742-194973`, assigns strand information for each gene, calculates the amplicon length, and writes the final BED file to `data/bed/drug_resistance_mad4.bed`.

2. The Bash chunk runs the Nextflow PathWeaver extraction pipeline. It activates the `nf-core` conda environment, moves to the directory containing the BAM files, and launches `pathweaver_extract_regions.nf`. The command uses the BED file from the first chunk, the Pf3D7 reference genome, Apptainer containers, and `-resume` so completed tasks are reused. The `--do_variant_calling` option tells the pipeline to run SeekDeep variant calling after extracting and clustering the target regions.

3. The final R chunk reads the SeekDeep amino-acid change summary and calculates country-level mutation prevalence. It first loads metadata containing sample country and `fws`, then cleans sample names in both the metadata and SeekDeep output so they can be joined. It keeps amino-acid calls with nonzero support (`AA_cnt != 0`), creates a per-sample mutation table, and then counts how many unique samples in each country carry each non-reference amino-acid change.

The object called `allelic_freq` is therefore a sample-level mutation prevalence table, not a read-weighted allele-frequency table. For each country, gene, and amino-acid position, the script calculates:

$$
  ext{mutation prevalence} = \frac{\text{number of samples carrying the mutant amino acid}}{\text{number of samples with a call at that amino-acid position}}
$$

Mixed infections or heterozygous-like calls are treated as carriers if the mutant amino acid has nonzero read support. For example, if a sample has both the reference amino acid and a mutant amino acid at the same position, the sample appears in the per-sample table with both calls and contributes one count to the mutant prevalence numerator. The sample is not weighted by `AA_freq`; a mutant present at 40% within a sample and a mutant present at 90% within a sample both count as one mutant-carrying sample in the prevalence calculation.

I run this script locally since there is some package issue here
```{r}
# install.packages("pak") if needed 
# install version v0.4.1 which introduces the tandem repeat work

# pak::pak("nickjhathaway/plasgenomicsutilsR@v0.4.1")

library(plasgenomicsutilsR)
library(dplyr)

# gff fnp, can be a link 
gff <- ensembl_gff_url("falciparum")        # or a local GFF path

# genes names to extract, remove PF from CARL as we'll prefix everything with pf which works to look up all these names
coronin <- c("PF3D7_1251200")
genes = c("MCA2", "KIC7", "KIC5", "KIC8","KIC9", "UBP1", "CARL","px1")

gene_location <- PF3D7_GENES |>
  filter(
    name %in% paste0("pf", tolower(genes))
  ) |>
  mutate(length = end - start)

# getting the short tandems to avoid with default setting, can change what is size is acceptable per
# repeating element size, default 1nuc > 10bp, dinuc > 12, trinuc > 21, above that > 50bp
# smaller repeats have more slippage so I typically avoid, but can change to get more uninterrupted regions 
# see help(tandem_repeats_to_avoid)
tr_to_avoid = tandem_repeats_to_avoid(pf3d7_tandem_repeats(), gap = 10)

# subtract the tandems from the genes 
gene_location_minus_tandems = bed_subtract(gene_location, tr_to_avoid, pad = 10)

# write to bed format that PathWeaver wants 
write_bed6(gene_location_minus_tandems, "gene_minus_tandems.bed", name_is_coords = T, meta_cols = c("gene_id", "name"))

# getting what amino acid positions are covered by those locations 
cds <- read_gff_cds(gff)
gene_location_minus_tandems_aa_positions = genomic_range_aa_positions(gene_location_minus_tandems, cds)

# get just exon locations for the genes of interest  
exons <- read_gff_features(gff, "exon", ids = gene_location$gene_id)
write_bed6(exons, "exons6.bed", name_is_coords = TRUE,
           meta_cols = c("gene_id", "name", "index"))

exons_aa <- genomic_range_aa_positions(exons, cds, keep = "hits")

# or subtract the tandem from exons 
exon_minus_tandems <- bed_subtract(exons, tr_to_avoid, pad = 10)
write_bed6(exon_minus_tandems, "exon_minus_tandems6.bed", name_is_coords = TRUE,
           meta_cols = c("gene_id", "name"))

exon_minus_tandems_aa <- genomic_range_aa_positions(exon_minus_tandems, cds, keep = "hits")

```

```{r,eval=FALSE}
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)


# I got the strand information from the gff file
resistance_mad4hatter <- read.csv("data/input/Pools.xlsx - Pool1B-Resitance+.csv") |> 
    filter(Category == "Resistance",!Gene %in% c("exo","pib7","pph")) |> 
    select(Gene,chr_malaria,amplicon_start,amplicon_end) |> 
  mutate(coord = paste(chr_malaria, amplicon_start, amplicon_end, sep = "-")) |> 
    mutate(strand = case_when(
        Gene == "aat1" ~ "-",
        Gene == "crt" ~ "+",
        Gene == "mdr1" ~ "+",
        Gene == "dhfr-ts" ~ "+",
        Gene == "dhps" ~ "+",
        Gene == "k13" ~ "-",
        grepl("pm", Gene) ~ "+",
        Gene == "ubp-1" ~ "+",
        Gene == "mdr2" ~ "-",
        Gene == "mdr2" ~ "+",
        Gene == "coronin" ~ "+",
        Gene == "arps10" ~ "+",
        Gene == "PF3D7_1322700" ~ "-",
        Gene == "fd" ~ "-",
        TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )) |> 
       # select(Gene, coord, strand) |>
    dplyr::rename(chr = chr_malaria,start = amplicon_start,end = amplicon_end) |> 
    mutate(length = end - start) %>%
  mutate(length = as.integer(length)) |> 
#   filter(length > 50) %>%
  select(chr, start, end, coord, length, strand)
write.table(
  resistance_mad4hatter %>% select(chr, start, end, coord, length, strand),
  "data/bed/drug_resistance_mad4.bed",
  sep = "\t",
  quote = FALSE,
  row.names = FALSE,
  col.names = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(ggplot2)

suppleme_fws <- read.csv(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/supplementary_Data/supp_fws_up.tsv",
  sep = "\t"
) %>%
  select(sample_id, Country, fws) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sample_id)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("-D0", "_D0", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("NG-A4488_", "", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_libLAN[0-9]+", "", Sample)) %>%
  select(Sample, Country, fws)

seekdeep_results_ubp <- read.csv(
  "output/seekdeep_ubp_kic/PathWeaverResults/variantCalls/reports/summary/AAChangesInfo.tsv.gz",
  sep = "\t"
) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("-D0", "_D0", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("NG-A4488_", "", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_libLAN[0-9]+", "", Sample)) %>%
  filter(AA_cnt != 0) %>%
  select(
    Sample,
    Gene,
    Gene_ID,
    reference_AA_pos,
    reference_AA,
    AA,
    is_reference,
    AA_freq,
    AA_cnt
  ) %>%
  # dplyr::rename(Read = AA_cnt)
  right_join(suppleme_fws, by = "Sample")
  
seekdeep_results_kic9 <- read.csv(
  "output/seekdeep_kic9/PathWeaverResults/variantCalls/reports/summary/AAChangesInfo.tsv.gz",
  sep = "\t"
) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("-D0", "_D0", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("NG-A4488_", "", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_libLAN[0-9]+", "", Sample)) %>%
  filter(AA_cnt != 0) %>%
  select(
    Sample,
    Gene,
    Gene_ID,
    reference_AA_pos,
    reference_AA,
    AA,
    is_reference,
    AA_freq,
    AA_cnt
  ) %>%
  # dplyr::rename(Read = AA_cnt)
  right_join(suppleme_fws, by = "Sample")
seekdeep_results <- read.csv(
  "output/seekdeep/PathWeaverResults/variantCalls/reports/summary/AAChangesInfo.tsv.gz",
  sep = "\t"
) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("-D0", "_D0", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("NG-A4488_", "", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_libLAN[0-9]+", "", Sample)) %>%
  filter(AA_cnt != 0) %>%
  select(
    Sample,
    Gene,
    Gene_ID,
    reference_AA_pos,
    reference_AA,
    AA,
    is_reference,
    AA_freq,
    AA_cnt
  ) %>%
  # dplyr::rename(Read = AA_cnt)
  right_join(suppleme_fws, by = "Sample") |> 
  # filter(Gene != "PX1") |> # the reason i remove this px1 here is that the bed file is from the one Nick send us not from the one tandem remove
  rbind(seekdeep_results_ubp) |> 
  rbind(seekdeep_results_kic9)
readr::write_tsv(seekdeep_results, "output/drug_resistance/seekdeep_results.tsv.gz")
  wide_sample <- seekdeep_results %>%
  mutate(
    mutation_status = ifelse(reference_AA == AA, "wildtype", "mutant"),
    mutation_test = ifelse(
      reference_AA == AA,
      paste0("0", "(", AA_freq, ")"),
      paste0(reference_AA, reference_AA_pos, AA, "(", AA_freq, ")")
    )
  ) %>%
  select(Sample, Gene, reference_AA_pos, mutation_test, Country) %>%
  group_by(Gene, reference_AA_pos, Sample, Country) %>%
  summarise(
    mutation_test = paste(unique(mutation_test), collapse = ";"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
  pivoting_result <- wide_sample %>%
    select(-Country) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Sample,
    values_from = mutation_test,
    values_fill = "NA"
  )
readr::write_tsv(pivoting_result, "output/drug_resistance/wide_sample_seekdeep_output_all_additional_variant.tsv")

country_n <- wide_sample %>%
  group_by(Country,Gene,reference_AA_pos) %>%
  summarise(
    total_samples = n_distinct(Sample),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Variant frequencies
mutation_prevalence_long <- seekdeep_results %>%
  mutate(
    mutation = paste0(reference_AA, reference_AA_pos, AA),
    aa_change = paste0(reference_AA, ">", AA)
  ) %>%
  group_by(
    Country,
    Gene,
    reference_AA_pos,
    mutation,
    aa_change,
    is_reference
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    n_samples = n_distinct(Sample),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(country_n, by = c("Country", "Gene", "reference_AA_pos")) %>%
  filter(is_reference == FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    freq = n_samples / total_samples,
    freq_label = paste0(
      round(freq, 3),
      " (",
      n_samples,
      "/",
      total_samples,
      ")"
    )
  )

allelic_freq <- mutation_prevalence_long %>%
  select(
    Gene,
    reference_AA_pos,
    mutation,
    aa_change,
    Country,
    freq_label
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Country,
    values_from = freq_label,
    values_fill = "0 (0/0)"
  ) %>%
  arrange(Gene, reference_AA_pos)
readr::write_tsv(allelic_freq, "output/drug_resistance/allelic_freq.tsv")
mutation_prevalence_plot <- mutation_prevalence_long %>%
  mutate(
    mutation_label = paste(Gene, mutation, sep = ": "),
    Country = factor(Country, levels = sort(unique(Country))),
    mutation_label = reorder(mutation_label, freq)
  )

ggplot(mutation_prevalence_plot, aes(x = Country, y = mutation_label, fill = freq)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#f7fbff",
    high = "#08306b",
    limits = c(0, 1),
    labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
    name = "Prevalence"
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Country",
    y = "Gene and amino-acid change",
    title = "Drug-resistance mutation prevalence by country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank()
  )

gene_prevalence_plot <- mutation_prevalence_long %>%
  group_by(Country, Gene) %>%
  summarise(
    freq = max(freq, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Country = factor(Country, levels = sort(unique(Country))),
    Gene = reorder(Gene, freq)
  )
```

## PX1 genotype annotation for iTOL

The following chunk creates an iTOL `DATASET_COLORSTRIP` annotation. Each tree tip is matched using the value in the `Sample` column, and the strip color represents the combined PX1 genotype at amino-acid positions 1222, 1701, and 1705. The tip labels in the Newick tree must exactly match these sample IDs. Haplotypes containing `NA` indicate that at least one target position did not have a genotype call; they are retained as separate categories and are not interpreted as wildtype.

```{r,eval=FALSE}
# i just remove out the south Asia samples 
px1_itol <- readr::read_tsv(
  "output/px1_genotype_result/px1_genotype_result.tsv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(Country.x %in% c("Thailand","India","Myanmar"))) %>%
  distinct(Sample, haplotype)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(px1_itol$Sample))

haplotypes <- sort(unique(px1_itol$haplotype))
haplotype_colors <- setNames(
  grDevices::hcl.colors(length(haplotypes), palette = "Dark 3"),
  haplotypes
)
haplotype_colors["WT/WT/WT"] <- "#BDBDBD"

itol_lines <- c(
  "DATASET_COLORSTRIP",
  "SEPARATOR TAB",
  "DATASET_LABEL\tPX1 genotype",
  "COLOR\t#000000",
  "STRIP_WIDTH\t50",
  "MARGIN\t5",
  "BORDER_WIDTH\t0",
  "SHOW_INTERNAL\t0",
  "LEGEND_TITLE\tPX1 genotype (1222/1701/1705)",
  paste("LEGEND_SHAPES", paste(rep(1, length(haplotypes)), collapse = "\t"), sep = "\t"),
  paste("LEGEND_COLORS", paste(haplotype_colors[haplotypes], collapse = "\t"), sep = "\t"),
  paste("LEGEND_LABELS", paste(haplotypes, collapse = "\t"), sep = "\t"),
  "DATA",
  paste(
    px1_itol$Sample,
    haplotype_colors[px1_itol$haplotype],
    px1_itol$haplotype,
    sep = "\t"
  )
)

itol_output <- "output/px1_genotype_result/px1_genotype_itol_colorstrip.txt"
writeLines(itol_lines, itol_output)
```

Upload `px1_genotype_itol_colorstrip.txt` to iTOL using **Datasets > Add dataset** after loading the neighbor-joining tree.


```{r}
genes <- c("CRT", "PX1","Kelch13")

gene_results <- list()

for (gene in genes) {

  gene_results[[gene]] <- seekdeep_results |>
    filter(Gene == gene) |>
    # arrange is_reference so reference allele is first when arranging
    arrange(desc(is_reference)) |>
    group_by(Sample, reference_AA_pos) |>
    summarise(
      # take the first reference_AA to avoid duplicate rows for overlapping references (e.g. position 1677 in PX1)
      reference_AA = first(reference_AA),
      # collapse unique AA alleles seen for this positioning
      AA = paste0(unique(AA), collapse = "/"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      aa_id = paste0(
        reference_AA,
        reference_AA_pos,
        ifelse(reference_AA != AA, AA, "")
      ),
      gene_pos = paste0(
        gene, "_",
        stringr::str_pad(reference_AA_pos, pad = "0", width = 3)
      )
    ) |>
    select(Sample, gene_pos, aa_id) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(
      names_from = gene_pos,
      values_from = aa_id
    )
}
```

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(patchwork)

# The haplotype grid, built once and reused by CRT and K13.
#
# `split` is a metadata column -- country here. Haplotypes are defined across every sample that
# is drawn, so one row is the same haplotype in both countries and the count panel shows how it
# divides; that is what makes a shared haplotype distinguishable from a country-specific one.
# `within` instead keeps only those countries and re-derives the haplotypes, which renumbers
# them, so use it for a per-country figure rather than to compare the two.
#
# The returned patchwork carries the number of haplotype rows as an `n_hap` attribute, since the
# page has to be tall enough for them.
aa_hap_plot <- function(collapsed, meta, split = "country", within = NULL, colors = NULL) {
  groups <- meta |>
    transmute(sample, split_group = as.character(.data[[split]])) |>
    distinct()

  dat <- collapsed |>
    ungroup() |>
    left_join(groups, by = "sample") |>
    # a sample with no metadata row is shown rather than dropped: losing it would quietly
    # shrink the counts the bar panel reports
    mutate(split_group = if_else(is.na(split_group), "unknown", split_group))

  if (!is.null(within)) {
    dat <- filter(dat, split_group %in% within)
    if (!nrow(dat))
      stop("no samples with ", split, " in ", paste(within, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
  }

  pos_levels <- sort(unique(dat$reference_AA_pos))

  # one haplotype string per sample (position:AA so missing positions can't silently align)
  hap_by_sample <- dat |>
    arrange(sample, reference_AA_pos) |>
    group_by(sample, split_group) |>
    summarise(haplotype = paste0(reference_AA_pos, ":", AA, collapse = "|"), .groups = "drop")

  # rows are ordered by the total, so the most common haplotype stays on top however it splits
  hap_totals <- hap_by_sample |>
    count(haplotype, name = "n") |>
    arrange(desc(n)) |>
    mutate(hap_id = paste0("H", row_number()),
           hap_lab = paste0(hap_id, " (n=", n, ")"))
  hap_order <- rev(hap_totals$hap_lab)

  lab <- function(d) mutate(d, hap_lab = factor(hap_lab, levels = hap_order))

  hap_by_group <- hap_by_sample |>
    count(haplotype, split_group, name = "n") |>
    left_join(select(hap_totals, haplotype, hap_lab), by = "haplotype") |>
    lab()

  hap_long <- dat |>
    left_join(select(hap_by_sample, sample, haplotype), by = "sample") |>
    left_join(select(hap_totals, haplotype, hap_lab), by = "haplotype") |>
    distinct(hap_lab, reference_AA_pos, reference_AA, AA) |>
    mutate(reference_AA_pos = factor(reference_AA_pos, levels = pos_levels)) |>
    lab()

  # the package palette by default, so these match the other figures. `colors` overrides it;
  # name it by level to hold a country to one colour across figures that draw different subsets,
  # which an unnamed vector cannot do since it is read in the order of the levels present here
  group_levels <- sort(unique(hap_by_group$split_group))
  group_colors <- if (is.null(colors)) plasgenomicsutilsR::color_palette(length(group_levels)) else colors
  if (is.null(names(group_colors))) {
    group_colors <- rep_len(group_colors, length(group_levels))
    names(group_colors) <- group_levels
  }

  p_grid <- ggplot(hap_long, aes(x = reference_AA_pos, y = hap_lab)) +
    geom_label(aes(label = AA, fill = AA != reference_AA),
               size = 3, linewidth = 0.2) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "white", `TRUE` = "#FDD9A0"), guide = "none") +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(x = "AA Position", y = "Haplotype")

  p_bar <- ggplot(hap_by_group, aes(x = n, y = hap_lab, fill = split_group)) +
    geom_col() +
    # the label is the total, so it reads the same whether or not the bar is stacked
    geom_text(data = lab(hap_totals), aes(x = n, y = hap_lab, label = n),
              inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = -0.25, size = 3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = group_colors) +
    scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.3))) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major.y = element_blank()) +
    labs(x = "N samples", fill = split)

  # a one-level legend says nothing the title does not, so name the group instead
  if (length(group_levels) < 2) {
    p_bar <- p_bar + guides(fill = "none")
    p <- p_grid + p_bar + plot_layout(widths = c(6, 1)) +
      plot_annotation(title = paste(group_levels, collapse = ", "))
  } else {
    p <- p_grid + p_bar + plot_layout(widths = c(6, 1), guides = "collect")
  }
  attr(p, "n_hap") <- nrow(hap_totals)
  p
}

# Per-country figures, sized from the combined one so the rows keep the same height.
hap_plot_by_group <- function(collapsed, meta, prefix, width, per_row, split = "country",
                              colors = NULL) {
  # levels taken from the samples actually drawn, not from every row of the metadata, so a
  # country with nothing in this gene's table is skipped instead of erroring
  drawn <- filter(meta, sample %in% unique(collapsed$sample))
  group_levels <- sort(unique(as.character(drawn[[split]])))
  # fix the palette over every level up front, so a country is the same colour in its own
  # figure as in the combined one -- left to itself each single-country plot would take the
  # first colour of the palette
  if (is.null(colors))
    colors <- setNames(plasgenomicsutilsR::color_palette(length(group_levels)), group_levels)

  for (g in group_levels) {
    p <- aa_hap_plot(collapsed, meta, split = split, within = g, colors = colors)
    cairo_pdf(paste0(prefix, "_", gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9]+", "_", g), ".pdf"),
              width = width, height = max(4, per_row * attr(p, "n_hap")))
    print(p)
    dev.off()
  }
}
```

```{r}
suppleme_fws <- read.csv(
  "/mnt/storage13/ahri/popgen_ethiopia_WGS/all_country_merged/WGS_Pf_Ethiopia_2024/supplementary_Data/supp_fws_up.tsv",
  sep = "\t"
) %>%
  select(sample_id, Country, fws) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sample_id)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("-D0", "_D0", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("NG-A4488_", "", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(sample = gsub("_libLAN[0-9]+", "", Sample)) %>%
  select(sample, Country) |> 
  dplyr::rename(country = Country) 
sample_meta <- suppleme_fws
crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo = readr::read_tsv("output/seekdeep_crt/PathWeaverResults/variantCalls/reports/summary/AAChangesInfo.tsv.gz") |>  mutate(Sample = gsub("_S[0-9]+$", "", sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("-D0", "_D0", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("NG-A4488_", "", Sample)) %>%
  mutate(Sample = gsub("_libLAN[0-9]+", "", Sample)) %>%
  filter(AA_cnt > 0)

min_within_sample_freq = 0.1

crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse = crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo %>% 
  filter(AA_freq >= min_within_sample_freq) |> 
  group_by(Sample, reference_AA_pos, reference_AA) %>% 
  arrange(desc(is_reference)) %>% 
  summarise(AA = paste0(AA, collapse = "/"), .groups = "drop") |> 
  filter(Sample %in% suppleme_fws$sample) |> 
  dplyr::rename(sample = Sample)

# drop samples called at fewer than this fraction of CRT positions
min_pos_called_frac = 0.8

n_crt_positions = n_distinct(crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse$reference_AA_pos)

crt_sample_missingness = crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse |> 
  group_by(sample) |> 
  summarise(n_called = n_distinct(reference_AA_pos), .groups = "drop") |> 
  mutate(frac_called = n_called / n_crt_positions,
         frac_missing = 1 - frac_called)

crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse = crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse |> 
  semi_join(filter(crt_sample_missingness, frac_called >= min_pos_called_frac), by = "sample")

crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse_sp = crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse %>% 
  mutate(aa_id = paste0(reference_AA, reference_AA_pos, ifelse(reference_AA != AA, AA, ""))) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(gene_pos = paste0("CRT_", stringr::str_pad(reference_AA_pos, pad = "0", width = 3))) %>% 
  select(sample, gene_pos, aa_id) %>% 
  spread(gene_pos, aa_id)

pfcrt_hap_plot = aa_hap_plot(crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse, sample_meta)

# the page has always been 30 inches for these rows; reuse that per-row height for the
# per-country figures, which have fewer haplotypes
pfcrt_hap_plot_per_row = 30 / attr(pfcrt_hap_plot, "n_hap")

cairo_pdf("pfcrt_hap_plot.pdf", width = 15, height = 30)
print(pfcrt_hap_plot)
dev.off()

hap_plot_by_group(crt_regions_pw_AAChangesInfo_collapse, sample_meta,
                  prefix = "pfcrt_hap_plot_thr_80", width = 15, per_row = pfcrt_hap_plot_per_row)
```
